events.title: Birth of Florence Nightingale
events.description: Florence Nightingale, the English social reformer and statistician, was born in Florence, Italy. She rose to prominence while managing nurses during the Crimean War and later founded the Nightingale Training School for nurses at St Thomas' Hospital in London.
events.significance: Considered the founder of modern nursing, she transformed hospital sanitation and healthcare practice and pioneered the use of statistical graphics in public health. International Nurses Day is celebrated on her birthday.

events.title: Lindbergh Baby Found Dead
events.description: The body of Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr., the 20-month-old son of aviator Charles Lindbergh, was discovered near the family's home in Hopewell, New Jersey, about two months after his kidnapping.
events.significance: The case, dubbed the 'Crime of the Century,' led to the Federal Kidnapping Act (the Lindbergh Law) and prompted major advances in forensic investigation and federal law enforcement.

events.title: Soviet Union Lifts the Berlin Blockade
events.description: The Soviet Union ended its blockade of West Berlin, which had begun in June 1948, reopening road, rail, and canal access to the western sectors of the city.
events.significance: The end of the blockade was an early Cold War victory for the Western Allies, whose Berlin Airlift had sustained the city, and it preceded the formal creation of West Germany later that month.

events.title: Berlin Airlift Success Concludes Blockade Crisis
events.description: With the blockade lifted, the Western Allies' airlift, which delivered over two million tons of supplies to West Berlin, was shown to have succeeded, though flights continued for several months to build up reserves.
events.significance: The airlift demonstrated Western resolve and logistical capability and helped solidify the NATO alliance formed in April 1949.

events.title: Axis Forces Surrender in Tunisia
events.description: Axis forces in North Africa, with the surrender of the remaining German and Italian troops in Tunisia, effectively ended the North African Campaign of World War II.
events.significance: The loss of North Africa removed Axis forces from the continent, opened the way for the Allied invasion of Sicily and Italy, and resulted in the capture of hundreds of thousands of Axis troops.
